changes.historical_text: This effect can be used during either player's turn. When your opponent activates a Trap Card, Tribute this face-up card to negate the activation of the Trap Card and destroy it.
changes.modern_text: This effect can be used during either player's turn. When your opponent activates a Trap Card, Tribute this face-up card to negate the activation of the Trap Card and destroy it.
changes.summary: Era damage-step legality encoded per card, not a text erratum: the goat script refuses the Tribute-to-negate activation during the Damage Step whenever this card is itself the attacker or the attack target (condition `not (Duel.GetCurrentPhase()==PHASE_DAMAGE and (Duel.GetAttacker()==c or Duel.GetAttackTarget()==c))`, upstream-annotated "Usable in the damage step only if it doesn't relate to battle"), while the modern script keeps EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP with no battle-relation test and so can negate a Trap in the Damage Step of its own battle. The rest of the diff is idiom: Cost.SelfTribute is literally the goat's inline IsReleasable/Duel.Release cost and Effect.IsTrapEffect is defined as IsActiveType(TYPE_TRAP) (both verified in CardScripts utility.lua). Chronology of the damage-step restriction is unresolved: no dated source in the packet or the shared briefs bounds it.

review.notes: Text-identical: the goat-entries.cdb text for 504700019 is byte-identical to the pinned modern cards.cdb text, and the Yugipedia errata page (revid 5386508) carries no English versions (and no other-language versions), so there is no printing available to date anything and no text transition to record; literal texts are carried on the change instead of lineage indices. I ran the engine-redundancy check the instructions call for: the GOAT rule profile (data/rule-profiles/tcg-goat.json: DUEL_6_STEP_BATLLE_STEP, DUEL_SINGLE_CHAIN_IN_DAMAGE_SUBSTEP, verified against the pinned ocgapi_constants.h) alters damage-step structure globally but does not decide which effects may be activated while their own card is in the battle, so the per-card script is not redundant with the rule profile and this stays 'ruling' rather than 'engine'.
